comments.author: @1rikkitikki
comments.text: *A bad credit event e.g. car repo, bankruptcy, late payments stays on your credit report for 7 years from the date the issue was established / determined to be a problem. A simple uncomplicated bankruptcy may take several months or more to process through the courts. The red flag destroying your credit report will remain on that report for seven years from the judgement date, not the day you stopped paying the bills. If it takes 6 months for your car to be repossessed, it stays on your credit report for seven years- not from when you started missing payments but from the date the repossession judgment is legally established by court order. What I’m trying to say is, yes a bad credit event diminishes your credit score for at least seven years but is almost always much longer.

comments.author: @OSUBUCKEYE1
comments.text: Back in 2002, I was working for a local dealership as a secretary and ended up getting a 2001 Ford Explorer sport. Beautiful SUV. I missed 2 payments for reasons I won't get into, but the way the repo company found me was they called my phone and said Fed Ex was trying to deliver a package and needed to know where to go. Now, the reason they did this was because where I lived at the time, the driveway of my house was hard to find because you had to go down a steep alley to get to my driveway. The driveway couldn't be seen from the front of the house. So, that's how they got me. I ended up getting it back 2 days later after paying what I owed and driving to the lot 3 hours away. That's the only time I've ever been behind on a car payment. The car I have now is nothing fancy, but it's paid off and gets me where I need to go. Would I like to have a newer car, absolutely.  But, I don't need it.

comments.text:
When your car gets repossessed, and the car is valued at say $20k, you owe $30k the finance company will still want to have you pay back the difference of $10k.  Doing damage to the car when it is being repossessed (or any time) will only bring the cash value of the car lower and the finance company will want even more money to be re-paid.  
Dumb Dumb Dumber.
If you can't afford the car just turn it in and you will be on the hook for less money, and your credit score won't be effected to the same degree if you waited until it was repossessed.
